scope: Review of the draft only; SQL stage proof, runtime and recovery evidence remain frozen. This is neither implementation authorization nor G2/G3 closure.

findings.topic: Executable v1 wire syntax and forest ownership
findings.evidence: Tags and prose do not define a closed per-tag schema, field names, required and forbidden fields, edge roles or representation of declarations and commands. Shared nodes have multiple lexical ancestries, and shared source occurrences create incompatible copy and trivia semantics. Existing frontend model is only a kind-only expression tree; it is not an adapter for this contract.
findings.resolution: Freeze a versioned JSON schema with duplicate-key rejection, exact fields, unique bounded IDs and no unknown properties. Use an ordered syntax forest: each expression node has exactly one parent or is exactly one body root, all nodes reachable, no cycles or sharing; declaration references are stable IDs and the existing e-graph DAG is a separate analysis artifact. Required envelope: version, signatures, predicates, facts, assertions, commands, nodes; each ordered declaration has id and name, each expression has id and tag. Signature has multiplicity and ordered fields; field has id, name, owner implicit in containing signature, ordered range signature IDs and supported range multiplicity. Predicate has ordered parameter records (binder id, name, signature id) and body root; fact/assertion have body root. Run targets predicate ID; check targets assertion ID; commands carry explicitly bounded scope options. Reference nodes carry signatureId, fieldId or binderId; predicate_call carries predicateId and ordered argument node IDs; unary tags have operand; binary tags have left and right; quantifier tags have binder record and body. Every tag has exactly those fields, exact cardinality and unique ownership. These are proposed freeze choices, not facts already proved. Add positive and malformed fixtures for every tag, root, arity, ID and field. Draft holes stay outside accepted IR.

findings.evidence: Field columns do not say whether the owner is included, n-ary field multiplicity syntax is unspecified, and predicate parameter multiplicity is absent. Parser acceptance alone cannot establish the intended dependency and multiplicity semantics.
findings.resolution: Define signature_ref schema [S], field_ref schema [owner, range1, ...], and variable_ref schema [S]. Each supported field has one or more range columns; specify the exact Alloy syntax and semantics for each permitted range multiplicity, including n-ary arrows, or reject combinations not demonstrably representable while retaining n-ary set fields. Parameter and quantifier binder semantics are exactly one atom of its declared signature; print explicit 'one' where needed and distinguish it from Alloy's default parameter multiplicity. Calls require argument count, exact schema and singleton multiplicity; if expression singleton cannot be established statically, restrict call arguments to singleton binders or reject. Set operations/equality/subset demand equal nonempty schemas; join matches endpoints and rejects empty output; product checks resulting arity cap; transpose is binary. Solver, not the nominal checker, establishes satisfiability. Verify parser AST and solver behavior for each field and parameter form, including empty and multi-atom cases.

findings.evidence: Draft occurrence_rules asserts Alloy parser byte intervals without evidence; the worker uses CompUtil.parseEverything_fromFile and does not implement source maps. Alloy positions and AST spans may be inclusive, line/column based, normalized, synthetic or omit parentheses; occurrence-for-occurrence reconstruction cannot be inferred from parser acceptance.
findings.resolution: Inspect the pinned Alloy parser and Pos implementation and empirically pin its actual coordinate base, end inclusivity, tab, CRLF, Unicode and file-reading behavior before selecting a conversion. Never assume UTF-8 byte intervals. Retain exact UTF-8 source, reject invalid encodings/surrogates, and explicitly convert observed coordinates to zero-based half-open UTF-16 only when boundaries and source correspondence are established; reject ambiguous or missing mappings. If parser AST erases syntax, use a separately specified concrete-syntax/token adapter or printer-generated structural anchors; do not invent positions. Define equality after parse(print(IR)) through an explicit total elaborator and alpha-renaming bijections for declaration/binder IDs, ordered operands and declared command normalization; prohibit parser rewrites from silently changing the model. Test every constructor, repeated expressions, precedence/parentheses, generated identifiers and command targets, Unicode supplementary and combining characters, tabs, CRLF, LF and boundary errors. Round-trip and source map correspondence remain trusted adapter claims until proved or differentially validated.

findings.evidence: The isolated formal draft groups operators and does not prove concrete wire decoding, stable-ID binding, parser/printer or runtime correspondence. Draft budgets exceed the existing 32768-byte SourcePolicy and one-worker service configuration; 10000 nodes and depth 128 have no demonstrated inherited-budget compliance.
findings.resolution: Before production changes freeze concrete tag/typing rules, trust boundary and exact propositions in a new isolated Lean model: finite syntax forest well-formedness and reachability, nonempty nominal schemas, all operator cases, exact declaration and binder lookup, call arguments and acyclic predicate dependencies, whole-module validation, and transition-level revision/receipt/rollback/replay/undo invariants. Prove soundness of the executable decision procedures relative to these definitions and include acceptance and denial witnesses; register exact files, assumptions, hashes and propositions, obtain six independent final-hash reviews and two clean builds. Keep Alloy, SQL isolation, Java/TypeScript, coordinates and accessibility as explicit trust/empirical obligations unless separately proved. Start with 32768 UTF-8 source bytes, at most 256 syntax nodes and depth 32 as proposed upper limits, intersect every inherited bound and require measurements; derive edge, declaration, output and request bounds and enforce limits before expensive allocation. Bounds must not silently relax existing gates.

findings.topic: Concrete acceptance, runtime and documentation evidence
findings.evidence: The existing worker parses and checks selected commands, while the draft requires entire-module validation, durable transaction semantics and complete palette behavior. Its test bullets do not specify a differential oracle or cover the requested Java/TypeScript documentation threshold.
findings.resolution: After proof freeze and builds, implement trusted adapters against the frozen IR and compare Java and TypeScript validator outcomes with exported Lean decision-oracle vectors for each valid/invalid operator, scope, arity, dependency and limits case; independently parse printed Alloy and compare elaborated normalized IR. Exercise transaction races, replay-before-stale, rollback and restart; test accessibility and all inherited gates independently. Specify exact canonical request serialization, successful receipt lookup ordering, expiry/active-window rules, principal recovery and failure-receipt policy before freeze. Apply the user's 30-line Java/TypeScript documentation requirement to all new or changed source, with a mechanical check whose exact rule and scope are frozen; do not claim tests prove unmodeled runtime refinement.
